title: I Enforced the Slack Status-Away Rule on the Manager Who Pinged Anyway

parts.text: I set Slack to away at 5:31 p.m. per the handbook rule my manager, Lila, had pasted into onboarding: respect away. At 5:33 she DMed a red-dot question about a deck. I was twenty-seven, analyst, holding a bus pass. I waited. She posted in the team channel that I was unresponsive. I screenshotted away, the handbook paste, the red-dot, and her channel note. Then I replied in-thread at 9:02 p.m. with those four images and no extra words. At 9:04 she asked me to take it to DMs because the channel had the VP.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The VP is in the channel with the handbook paste and the away screenshot.

social.video_title: She pasted respect away and red-dotted me two minutes later — Part 1/2
social.description: Bus pass, 5:33 ping, unresponsive in the team channel. Four images at 9:02. Would you have answered the red dot?

parts.text: I left it in the channel. The VP reacted with eyes. Lila scheduled questions before 5. Away started meaning away. I still do the deck, in hours. Red dots are not fires. Handbooks are copy-paste until they are evidence. I ride the bus without Slack in my pocket. The status stays green only when I am.

social.video_title: The VP's eyes emoji did the management — Part 2/2
social.description: Left in channel, questions before 5, pocket without Slack. Was unresponsive a status?
